title: codemeta-drift mapping export
description: Where each CodeMeta term sits in each metadata format, read from one CodeMeta release (mapping-<codemeta_tag>.json). A row says where a value is, never how it is spelled: SPDX URL or id, ORCID URL or bare iD, 'Family, Given' and DOI forms are the consumer's business. Fields this schema does not define are allowed, so a reader that knows an older minor accepts a newer file. Contract and compatibility rules: docs/mapping-export.md.

schema_version.description: 'MAJOR.MINOR' of this schema. A consumer reads the major before anything else and stops on one it does not know. A minor adds optional fields, formats or terms and never changes what an existing field means.

codemeta_tag.description: The codemeta/codemeta tag the crosswalk rows were read from, such as '3.1'.

generator.description: The tool that wrote the file and its version. A hand-written file says so in a local version label, such as '0.1.0+hand'.

rows.description: One row per (format, term). A pair appears at most once; JSON Schema cannot say that, so consumers check it.

format.description: Stable format id: cff-1.2.0, codemeta, zenodo, pep621, cargo, npm. A versioned format puts its version in the id.

term.description: A CodeMeta term (name, version, author, license, identifier, codeRepository, description, keywords), or a person sub-term qualified by the term it sits under: author.givenName, author.familyName, author.@id (ORCID).

path.description: Where the value sits in the format's file, or null when the format has no place for it. Grammar: steps joined by '.'; a step is a key, a key followed by '[]' (each element of a list), or a key followed by '[k=v]' (each element whose k equals v). A key may contain letters, digits, '_' and '-', and may start with '@'. ' | ' separates alternatives, read left to right: the first that exists wins. A sub-term path is absolute and starts with its parent term's path. Examples: package.keywords, authors[].given-names, identifiers[type=doi].value, project.urls.Source | project.urls.Repository.

source.description: Why the row says what it says. 'crosswalk:<file>@<tag>' when the path reads the cell of that CodeMeta crosswalk; 'curated:<reason>' when the row departs from the crosswalk or the crosswalk has no cell.

see_also.description: Upstream issue or pull request that reports the crosswalk cell this row departs from.

comment.description: Free text for a human reader. Never machine-read.
